1) Network topology: do we need a VPC peering (private) or is PrivateLink the recommended approach for the AWS private listing flow when the ISV (NimbleOps) hosts a managed bundle?
2) Entitlement propagation: if the listing is a private offer, what signal does Redwood receive from the cloud marketplace to validate seats vs. a traditional SaaS license key?

We're drafting a short pilot SOW and would like to align on the technical wiring so we don't have to rework the Document. Can you loop in the platform/marketplace engineer who owns the Private listing integrations?

Alex — thanks for the clear questions. High level answers up front:

• Network: PrivateLink is our preferred, lowest-friction option for AWS private offers because it avoids cross-account VPC peering and gives you control over endpoint policies. We do support VPC peering where customers require direct peering for latency reasons, but that usually adds networking ops overhead for the ISV.

• Entitlement: for private offers we validate marketplace entitlements via the cloud's entitlement API (Marketplace Metering/Entitlement). We reconcile entitlements back to Redwood tenant IDs during purchase webhook processing — essentially marketplace order -> entitlement token -> Redwood mapping.

I'll loop Ben (partnerships) and Olga (engineering/marketplace evidence) to confirm implementation details and capture any edge cases we need in the SOW.

Proposed next step: quick 30m sync Tue 4/20 to walk the arch and confirm what goes into the SOW (pilot success criteria + deployment steps). Does 9:30am PT work for you?

—Karthik
